entry.title: What Fixing My Aunt’s Laptop Taught Me About Data Boundaries at Home
entry.summary:
Last month I spent a Saturday afternoon cleaning up my aunt’s laptop, and it turned into one of the more interesting security conversations I’ve had all year. Nothing dramatic happened, no malware popup, no ransom note. It was just the small stuff: three antivirus trials fighting each other, a browser with too many extensions, and a Downloads folder that looked like a landfill. I’ve noticed that helping relatives with tech is its own strange exercise. At work I can run a scan, check policy settings, maybe pull logs if something looks off. At her kitchen table I had none of that, and honestly I didn’t need most of it.
Here’s what struck me most: her laptop held more sensitive material than I expected. Tax documents from years back, scans of her passport, a folder of passwords she kept in a…

entry.title: Building Marlo: An Open-Source AI CMO for Founders and Startups
entry.summary: As founders, we spend countless hours building products, fixing bugs, and talking to customers. But when it comes to marketing, things get complicated quickly. You need to research competitors, find keywords, write blog posts, create content for LinkedIn and X, engage on Reddit, optimize SEO, generate leads, and keep everything consistent. Most founders either spend too much time on marketing or can't afford a dedicated team. That's why I built Marlo. What is Marlo? Marlo is an open-source AI CMO that helps founders and startups automate marketing research, strategy, and execution. Instead of using multiple tools, Marlo combines everything into one platform powered by specialized AI agents. What Marlo Can Do Most AI marketing tools are black boxes. I wanted Marlo to be: Open and transparent You own your data, choose your models, and extend the platform based on your needs. Who Is Marlo For? My vision is simple: Every founder should have access to an AI-powered marketing team without paying agency prices or juggling dozens of disconnected tools. Marlo is still evolving, and I'm actively looking for feedback from builders, marketers, and early adopters. If you're interested in AI-powered growth, open-source software, or marketing automation, I'd love to hear your thoughts. 🚀 Try Marlo: https://marlo.mlforge.in ⭐ GitHub: https://github.com/Kumar2421/marlo-self-hosted-ai-cmo

entry.title: How we monitor websites and servers before problems reach customers
entry.summary:
Short answer
We monitor websites and servers on several levels: whether the site responds from the outside, how loaded the server is, what the logs say and whether backups exist. The goal is to learn about a problem from our own monitoring, not from a client calling to say the site won't load. When we say customers, we also mean our clients' customers. The person who can't complete an order. The enquiry that never reaches anyone. The page that takes 15 seconds to load, so the visitor closes the tab. This is the first level, and we handle it with Uptime Kuma.
